questions.q: What central idea does Ford draw from comparing his first car with the Model T?
options: Perfecting one good idea beats hunting for new ones
Redesigning a car from scratch every few years pays off
Building cars for farm work matters more than speed
Learning mechanics from books beats tinkering by hand
questions.explain: He says it is better to concentrate on perfecting a good idea; one idea at a time is enough.

questions.q: How old was Ford when he saw the road engine?
options: Eight
Twelve
Fifteen
Twenty

questions.q: Who made the road engine he met?
options: Ford Motor Company of Dearborn, Michigan
Detroit Steam Works of Wayne County, Michigan
Nichols, Shepard & Company of Battle Creek
Oliver Plow Works of South Bend, Indiana
questions.explain: It was made by Nichols, Shepard & Company of Battle Creek.

questions.q: How many miles per hour could his first buggy reach?
options: Ten
Fifteen
Thirty
Twenty
questions.explain: The two-cylinder buggy would make twenty miles an hour.

questions.q: What does Ford imply about his family's early circumstances?
options: They were very poor, as the legend claims
They were prosperous by Michigan farm standards
They were wealthy owners of many large estates
They had lost most of the farm to debts
questions.explain: He calls the poverty a legend and says they were prosperous for Michigan farmers.
